rationale: PINS the `exports` relationship, which this lane never published. Before it, the analyzer filled ParseResult.exports (597 ExportInfo entries in 387 files at 400 corpus files) and emitted NO relationship of the type, so the one label that states "this module offers this name" was stored and compared against nothing — the shape 12 lanes shared fleet-wide. Three separate things are pinned here, and each was measured first. (1) The SOURCE is the module: the full CHAINED package path `com.example.exports`, joined from the two `package` clauses. metadata.packageName holds only the LAST clause (`exports`) on every multi-clause file — 308 of 600 corpus files — so an edge built on that field would name a package no reference site spells. (2) The SURFACE is the implicit one: every public top-level declaration, and NOT a private top-level class. (3) A companion pair declared object-first publishes exactly ONE edge. The ExportInfo array's object-suppression is order-dependent (Contexts.scala:2003 `object ContextMode`, :2109 `class ContextMode` — 42 repeated names per 883 entries at 600 files), and without the dedupe that pair becomes two edges for one fact. expectRelationshipCount pins the count; expectSymbolCount pins that the two SYMBOLS were not merged, because a surface edge is a statement about visibility, not about identity. The Scala 3 clauses pin the reader: a plain path, plain selectors, a RENAMED selector (`Delta => Renamed` introduces `Renamed`, which is the name bound HERE — `Delta` is only reachable under it), and a given selector. The two wildcard clauses are pinned as FORBIDDEN: `export other.module.*` and `export other.module.given` re-export a set the clause does not name, so there is no name to publish, and enumerating imagined members would be exactly the fabricated edge the ontology gate exists to catch.
